Context
-------
Read .github/copilot-instructions.md and the newest
feedback/airgap-run-*.md first.

This task runs on the connected upstream machine only. It updates the
repository's packaging, cleanup, and preparation artifacts. Do not
access the learner VM, run provisioning scripts against it, or claim
that any VM-side operation has passed.

The learner VM is RHEL 8.6. It will be provisioned on the airgapped
network, where it can reach Artifactory during setup. Artifactory
serves container images from:

  ${ART_HOST}/artifactory/docker-registry

The registry endpoint serves the image paths for docker.io, ghcr.io,
quay.io, and registry.k8s.io. Pulls are anonymous. The VM must be
fully preloaded before it is handed to attendees; it must not depend
on Artifactory or any other network service at runtime.

The repository is transferred as a ZIP. Do not require Git, Git LFS,
or an online Git service on the learner VM. Large non-container
artifacts may be transferred separately by an approved file-transfer
method.

Decisions
---------
1. Do not store large release binaries or container-image archives in
   ordinary Git history. DELETE the ones currently committed
   (see Task 1 for the list) as part of this task.
2. The primary k3s system-image path is to pull images from Artifactory
   during provisioning, after configuring k3s registry mirrors and CA
   trust, then verify they are present in k3s containerd storage.
3. The k3s airgap image tarball is an optional fallback, not a required
   artifact. It may be supplied separately if Artifactory-based
   installation proves unreliable. It is NOT committed to Git.
4. The k3s executable is a separate transfer payload. It is NOT
   committed to Git. Do not assume Artifactory provides a generic-file
   proxy for GitHub releases.
5. Docker Compose is not used by any workshop. Its vendored binary is
   REMOVED from the repository in this task, along with every
   reference to it. Do not make it a prerequisite for VM setup or
   diagnosis.
6. The repo ZIP and the separate payload archive (k3s binary, optional
   airgap tarball) each have a SHA-256 manifest and documented
   transfer/verification steps.
7. Removal of obsolete files is DESTRUCTIVE and therefore ordered: the
   replacement payload is fetched and verified BEFORE any working-tree
   deletion. If a fetch fails, nothing is removed. The existing freeze
   tag is the recovery path.

Objective
---------
Refactor the online-side repo so a ZIP can be transferred without
large binaries, remove the obsolete large files from the working tree,
and give the VM an install-time path to retrieve container images from
Artifactory plus a documented path for separately-transferred payloads.

Deliverables
------------
- scripts/dev/obsolete-artifacts.txt      NEW (removal manifest)
- scripts/dev/package-vm-transfer.sh      NEW (packager + cleanup)
- content/vendor/README.md                NEW
- content/vendor/k3s/SHA256SUMS           small manifest only
- scripts/00-diagnose.sh                  version bump (v3 -> v4)
- lab-vm.conf                             only where necessary
- README-FIRST.md                         updated
- versions.lock                           updated
- .gitignore                              updated
- content/extracted/vendored-files.txt    updated
- REMOVED from the working tree: the obsolete files per Task 1
- feedback/airgap-run-*.md                left unchanged

Task 1 — audit large tracked artifacts and write the removal manifest
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Inspect tracked files under content/ and identify files larger than
25 MiB. Print a table:

  path | size | required? | proposed delivery | action

Include at minimum:
  - content/bin/docker-compose-v2 and its .sha256
      action: REMOVE. No workshop uses Compose; do not retain it.
  - content/vendor/k3s/k3s (the binary, ~70 MB)
      action: REMOVE from Git. Re-supplied by package-vm-transfer.sh
      into the payload archive.
  - content/vendor/k3s/k3s-airgap-images-amd64.tar.zst (~300 MB)
      action: REMOVE from Git. Optional; re-supplied only when
      package-vm-transfer.sh is run with --include-k3s-airgap-tarball.
  - content/vendor/k3s/install.sh (~50 KB) and
    content/vendor/k3s/k3s-selinux-1.6-1.el8.noarch.rpm (~20 KB)
      action: KEEP. Small enough for Git.

Write scripts/dev/obsolete-artifacts.txt — a committed manifest, one
line per file, in this format:

  <repo-relative path> | <reason obsolete> | <replacement delivery>

Example lines:
  content/bin/docker-compose-v2 | unused by any lab; zero compose usage in recon | removed, no replacement
  content/bin/docker-compose-v2.sha256 | same | removed, no replacement
  content/vendor/k3s/k3s | >25 MiB binary; separate payload per decision 4 | payload archive: k3s/k3s
  content/vendor/k3s/k3s-airgap-images-amd64.tar.zst | >25 MiB; optional fallback per decision 3 | payload archive: k3s/k3s-airgap-images-amd64.tar.zst (opt-in)

This manifest is the ONLY source the packager may delete from. Do not
delete anything not listed. Do not add a path to the manifest without
verifying (a) it is tracked, (b) it is >25 MiB unless in the KEEP
exceptions above, and (c) a replacement is available or the file is
genuinely unused.

Do NOT delete any source until Task 2 has successfully packaged and
verified its replacement.

Task 2 — online payload packager with ordered cleanup
-----------------------------------------------------
Implement scripts/dev/package-vm-transfer.sh. This script runs on the
connected upstream machine. Phases run IN ORDER. Any failure aborts
before the next phase; the working tree is not modified until Phase D
succeeds.

Flags:
  --dry-run                      print every action, change nothing
  --include-k3s-airgap-tarball   also fetch and package the fallback
                                 tarball
  --no-clean                     skip Phase D (packaging still runs)
  --clean-obsolete-only          run Phases A-D and stop (no packaging)
  --refresh                      re-fetch pinned artifacts even if
                                 cached locally (must re-verify SHA)
  --out DIR                      default dist/o11y-lab-vm-transfer/

PHASE A — AUDIT
  Read scripts/dev/obsolete-artifacts.txt. For each entry, assert the
  path exists and is tracked (git ls-files). Report:
    - files to be removed
    - replacement delivery for each
    - total bytes recovered
  Abort with a fix-hint if any manifest path is not tracked or does
  not exist.

PHASE B — FETCH AND VERIFY REPLACEMENTS (nothing on disk is touched)
  For every replacement that the payload must carry:
    - k3s binary: pinned version from versions.lock; fetch from the
      pinned official release URL on THIS connected machine
    - k3s airgap tarball: only if --include-k3s-airgap-tarball
    - anything else listed in the manifest's replacement column
  Verify each against the pinned SHA-256 in versions.lock BEFORE
  proceeding. On mismatch: FATAL, no removal, print expected vs
  actual.
  If the artifact is already cached locally in the payload staging
  area with a matching SHA, reuse it (unless --refresh).
  Abort if a REQUIRED artifact cannot be fetched or verified.

PHASE C — PACKAGE
  1. Build the repository ZIP from the current tracked source and
     workshop content, EXCLUDING:
       .git/, .git/lfs/, dist/, generated logs/caches, and any path
       listed in scripts/dev/obsolete-artifacts.txt
     The ZIP reflects the state AFTER Phase D (i.e. without obsolete
     files) — build it from a staging copy taken after removal, or
     build it in Phase E; document the ordering choice in the script
     header.
  2. Build the payload archive containing only:
       - the verified k3s binary (REQUIRED)
       - the verified k3s airgap tarball (OPTIONAL; only with the flag)
     Store under dist/o11y-lab-vm-transfer/payload/.
  3. Write payload manifest: relative path | version | source URL |
     SHA-256 | REQUIRED|OPTIONAL | expected destination on the VM.
     Destination for the k3s binary: /usr/local/bin/k3s (0700 root)
     as installed by script 45. For the tarball:
     /var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/images/ before first k3s start.
  4. Write SHA-256 files for the repository ZIP and payload archive.

PHASE D — REMOVE OBSOLETE FILES (destructive; gated on B success)
  Only runs if Phases A-C succeeded (or --clean-obsolete-only).
  For each manifest path:
    - git rm -- <path>          (tracks the removal as a diff)
  Then update .gitignore to add SPECIFIC paths under
  content/vendor/k3s/ and content/bin/ so re-fetching does not
  accidentally re-commit them. Use explicit paths, not broad
  patterns that could hide legitimate content.
  Print the exact git diff --stat of removals.
  Do NOT commit. Leaving the removal staged (or unstaged, respecting
  the repo's conventions — check how prior commits were structured)
  lets the operator review the diff and choose the commit message.
  The freeze tag is the recovery path if the removal needs undoing.

PHASE E — SUMMARY
  Print:
    - repo ZIP: filename, byte size, SHA-256
    - payload archive: filename, byte size, SHA-256
    - removed files: count, total bytes
    - obsolete-manifest resolutions
    - the exact operator verification commands for the receiving side:
        sha256sum -c <repo-zip>.sha256
        sha256sum -c <payload>.sha256
    - the sequence the operator runs on the VM after transfer
      (extract ZIP, verify, then provisioning scripts)

The script must not place large artifacts back into Git at any point.
Update .gitignore to ignore dist/ and the payload staging directory.
Do not ignore source manifests or checksum files.

Task 3 — Artifactory-based k3s system images
-------------------------------------------
Update the k3s installation design and VM-side operator documentation.
Do not write the full provisioning scripts in this task.

Document the intended sequence:
1. Configure CA trust for the Artifactory registry host.
2. Write /etc/rancher/k3s/registries.yaml before starting k3s,
   mirroring registry.k8s.io and docker.io to the Artifactory
   endpoint.
3. Install the pinned k3s binary from the separately-transferred
   payload and verify its SHA-256.
4. Start k3s while Artifactory is reachable so required system images
   can be pulled.
5. Verify system pods are Ready and inspect the k3s image store.
6. Later, provision workshop images into the separate k3s containerd
   store and verify them with Artifactory access blocked.

Important:
- Use the registry configuration format supported by the pinned k3s
  release. Verify it against that release's documentation/source.
- Do not assume `k3s ctr` uses `registries.yaml` mirror configuration.
  Verify the exact supported pull mechanism for the pinned k3s
  version. Document the chosen method and its diagnostics.
- The earlier online registry probe returned HTTP 000 because the
  online machine could not resolve artifactory.internal. Treat that
  as "not probed", not as evidence of an image miss.
- Do not claim Artifactory-based k3s pulls are verified until the
  operator has tested them on the airgapped network.

If --include-k3s-airgap-tarball was used, document the fallback: copy
the tarball to the k3s agent image directory before first k3s start,
verify its checksum, and explain it avoids pulling k3s system images
during bootstrap. Not mandatory.

Task 4 — update 00-diagnose.sh and lab-vm.conf
----------------------------------------------
Read the current versions before editing. Bump the script version and
add the required one-line change comment.

Update scripts/00-diagnose.sh (v3 -> v4) so it:
- NO LONGER checks content/bin/docker-compose-v2 or its checksum.
  Grep the script for every compose reference and remove it.
- Reports k3s binary payload presence as:
    present and checksum-valid;
    absent, with a clear instruction to transfer/extract the payload;
    checksum-invalid, with expected and actual hashes.
- Treats the k3s airgap tarball as optional:
    present and valid: report available fallback;
    absent: report that provisioning will use Artifactory pulls.
- Keeps checking that content/extracted/{commands.json,
  curated.json, external-images.txt} exist.
- Does NOT claim the registry probe passed if its previous result was
  HTTP 000.
- Remains read-only in normal mode and always exits 0.
- Preserves --selftest and the report-block protocol.

Update lab-vm.conf only as needed. REQUIRED to remain:
- WORKSHOP_USER="engineer"    (assert in 10-preflight; fix-hint if
                               absent — this was a known 10r gap)
- PASSWORDLESS_SUDO="yes"
- DOCS_PORT="8090"
- DOCKER_REGISTRY="${ART_HOST}/artifactory/docker-registry"
Also update the comment that still refers to "workshop account" to
name engineer.

Do not add Compose or Docker CE variables. Remove any comment that
references the compose binary.

Task 5 — update docs
--------------------
Update README-FIRST.md and create content/vendor/README.md, documenting:

- The repository ZIP and the payload archive are transferred
  separately.
- Exact checksum-verification commands to run after transfer.
- The expected learner-VM payload staging directory.
- How to copy/extract the k3s binary and optional tarball.
- Artifactory is used during provisioning to obtain container images.
- No container image or other dependency is pulled at attendee
  runtime.
- The optional tarball fallback and when to use it.
- The k3s and podman image stores are separate.
- Large payloads are generated by the online packaging script, not
  committed.
- The obsolete-files removal (Task 1/D) and how to revert it (check
  out the freeze tag).

Do not use placeholder commands such as `curl | sh`. Do not include
credentials, tokens, or private hostnames beyond values already in
lab-vm.conf.

Task 6 — integrity and grep audits (must ALL pass)
--------------------------------------------------
- k3s binary SHA in the payload manifest matches versions.lock.
- Optional tarball SHA in the payload manifest matches versions.lock.
- Manifest labels REQUIRED vs OPTIONAL correctly.
- versions.lock and content/extracted/vendored-files.txt updated to
  describe the new delivery model (no claim that large artifacts are
  committed).
- No remaining reference to content/bin/docker-compose-v2 anywhere in
  the repo:
      grep -rn "docker-compose-v2" . --exclude-dir=.git
      grep -rn "docker-compose " scripts/ README-FIRST.md
      grep -rn "content/bin" scripts/ README-FIRST.md content/vendor/README.md
  All must be empty.
- The obsolete-artifacts manifest lists only paths that no longer
  exist in the working tree (post-removal) OR are staged for removal:
      for each path in scripts/dev/obsolete-artifacts.txt, assert it
      is either deleted or listed as `git rm --cached` pending.
- No large file (>25 MiB) remains tracked under content/:
      git ls-files -z content/ | xargs -0 -I{} sh -c \
        'test "$(stat -c%s "{}")" -gt 26214400 && echo "{}"'
  must produce no output except the KEEP exceptions (install.sh, the
  selinux RPM).

Acceptance
----------
1. Dispatch: print --dry-run output for Phases A-D. This is the
   operator's review artifact before any real run.
2. paste scripts/dev/obsolete-artifacts.txt in full.
3. paste git diff --stat of the removals (Phase D).
4. paste the Phase E summary: repo ZIP + payload archive SHA-256s,
   removed-file count and total bytes, and the operator verification
   commands.
5. paste grep-audit results: all three greps empty, the "no large
   tracked files" check empty except KEEP exceptions.
6. State explicitly: the working tree now has the removals staged but
   NOT committed — the operator reviews and commits.
7. State: everything ran online; the learner VM was not accessed; no
   provisioning script was executed.
